items.title: Cannot pack perl PAR::Packer executables
items.body:
<!---

IF YOU REMOVE THIS TEMPLATE WE WILL CLOSE YOUR ISSUE WITHOUT RESPONSE.
Just read it and fill in the details we're asking, it saves so much of our time. Thanks!

-->

## What's the problem (or question)?
<!--- If describing a bug, tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->
<!--- If suggesting a change/improvement, explain the difference from current behavior -->
When I try to pack a 32 bit Windows executable generated with PAR::Packer using upx 3.95 (32 bit and 64 bit) the resulting executable is successfully shrunk and packed. However when I run the executable I get the following error messages:
IO error: reading header signature :
 at -e line 603.
IO error: reading header signature :
 at -e line 595.
...
mkdir C:\Users\ADMINI~1\AppData\Local\Temp\par-41646d696e6973747261746f72\cache-287b72321943f32b96f721e8c8356c9fd1949556\inc\script\: File exists; Cannot create a file when that file already exists at C:/strawberry/perl/vendor/lib/Archive/Z
ip/Archive.pm line 196.

## What should have happened?
<!--- If you're describing a bug, tell us what should happen -->
<!--- If you're suggesting a change/improvement, tell us how it should work -->
The executable should successfully unpack the resources to the temp dir and run.

## Do you have an idea for a solution?
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug, -->
<!--- or ideas how to implement the addition or change -->
I suspect the upx packed exe can't read (I/O error) the pp packed resources in order create and populate the directories properly, and zero length files are created instead.
Maybe need the PAR::Packer team to improve compatibility with upx.

## How can we reproduce the issue?
<!--- Provide unambiguous set of steps to reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant -->
1. Install strawberry perl 32 bit on Windows 10 (use the add perl to environment and path option) 
2. run cpan install pp to install PAR::Packer and dependencies
3. Create a simple helloworld.pl file
4. pp helloworld.pl -o helloworld.exe
5. install upx 3.95w 32 bit
6. upx helloworld.exe
7. Run the generated helloworld.exe on another system or the same system.

Note: you won't get an error from running the upx packed exe if you run the non-upx packed pp generated exe first on the target system because that non-upx exe will successfully create and populate the temp directories.
Note 2: you will get an error if you run the non-upx packed exe after running the upx packed exe first since the non-upx exe does not overwrite the zero length files with directories. You will have to delete the temporary par directories in the temp folder to successfully run the non-upx exe.

## Please tell us details about your environment.
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
* UPX version used (`upx --version`):
3.95w and 3.91w
* Host Operating System and version:
Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.17763.615] Windows 10 64 bit
Strawberry Perl 5.30.0.1-32bit
* Host CPU architecture:
Intel x86 64 bit
* Target Operating System and version:
Microsoft Windows [Version 6.1.7600] Windows Server 2008 R2 64 bit
* Target CPU architecture:
Intel x86 64 bit

## What's the problem (or question)?
I wonder if UPX can keep original EXE header (including size and contents) so target program can still able to use contents in EXE header.

## What should have happened?
Currently, UPX replaced EXE header with its own one.

## Do you have an idea for a solution?
Add a switch to keep original EXE header, and try best to keep it unless there is a need for unpacking stub use.
